title: Capstone: filter the even numbers into a new list
idea: GUIDED CAPSTONE. Build a NEW list by appending only items that pass a test — the filter pattern.
problem: From [3, 8, 5, 12, 7], collect just the even numbers into a new list [8, 12].

exercises.prompt: PROBLEM: collect the evens from [3, 8, 5, 12, 7]. OUTPUT is...
options: A new list of the even numbers
exercises.explanation: Output is a NEW list, not a count or sum. Filtering keeps the items that pass.

exercises.prompt: How do we test 'is this number even'?
exercises.explanation: Even means remainder 0 when divided by 2. You derived this in the number-puzzles unit.

exercises.prompt: Example by hand: which of 3, 8, 5, 12, 7 are even?
exercises.explanation: 8 and 12 are even; the rest are odd. The filtered list should be [8, 12].

exercises.prompt: The filtered list should keep the evens in the SAME order they appeared in the original.
exercises.explanation: Yes — appending as we scan preserves order, giving [8, 12]. That's our check.

exercises.prompt: Plan the filter. Order the steps.
blocks: If the number is even, append it to the new list
For each number in the original
The new list is the result
exercises.explanation: Empty list, scan, append on pass. Building a fresh list is the heart of the filter pattern.

exercises.prompt: Which method adds an item to the end of the new list?
exercises.explanation: append() grows a list by one item. We call it only when the number passes the even test.

exercises.prompt: Code the filter. Arrange the lines.
exercises.explanation: Start evens empty, loop, test even, append inside the if. Order and indentation both matter.
append(number) adds the passing number to evens. Result: [8, 12].

exercises.prompt: Run it: prints [8, 12]. Hand said [8, 12]. Verdict?
exercises.explanation: Matches. Only evens were appended, in original order.

exercises.prompt: Re-run on [2, 4, 6]. What's the filtered list?
exercises.explanation: Every item passes, so all are appended. Filter keeps as many as qualify — here, all of them.
